cards.front: Every Java statement must end with which character?
cards.extra: A statement is a complete unit of execution and ends with ;. Control-flow headers (if, for, while) and blocks { ... } are not statements themselves, so they take no semicolon — if (x) return; needs one only because of the return inside.

cards.text: Java is {{c1::case-sensitive}}: Name and name are two different identifiers.
cards.extra: Java distinguishes Name from name everywhere — variables, methods, classes, even file names. System resolves; system does not.

cards.front: Which comment syntax does Java use for a single line?
cards.extra: // runs to the end of the line; /* ... */ spans lines but does not nest; /** ... */ is a Javadoc comment that the javadoc tool turns into HTML documentation.
Class and interface names are nouns in PascalCase — BankAccount, Runnable. It is convention, not a compiler rule: class bankAccount compiles and still makes reviewers unhappy.
Variables and methods start lowercase and capitalise each later word — accountBalance, withdraw(). Underscores are reserved for constants.
A static final field is a constant, so it is written in capitals with underscores — MAX_RETRIES. That makes constants visually distinct from ordinary fields.

cards.front: What is the entry-point signature of a Java application?
cards.extra: public so the launcher can call it, static so no instance is needed, void so nothing is returned, and String[] args carries command-line arguments. The launcher looks for exactly main(String[]) and silently skips anything else.

cards.question: Which three layers does this diagram show, outermost to innermost?
cards.extra: JDK = JRE + development tools; JRE = JVM + core class libraries; the JVM loads, verifies, interprets/JITs and garbage-collects.

cards.front:
What does this print?

int sum = 0;
for (int i = 1; i <= 4; i++) {
    sum += i;
}
System.out.println(sum);
cards.extra: The loop adds 1+2+3+4. The condition i <= 4 is tested before each iteration, so the body runs while i is 1..4 and then exits.
